A 68-year-old gentleman presents for clinical review, his medical background including coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, and atrial fibrillation. Divorced but currently residing with his partner, he recently retired from carpentry and maintains an active routine centred around gardening, though he admits to no formal exercise programme. Alcohol intake is moderate at nine units weekly, and he is a current smoker with a 17 pack-year history, but he reports no lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of zero. He notes occasional mild tinnitus and mentions a routine chest X-ray performed recently for occupational health clearance, which was unremarkable. He has noted some hearing difficulty and prefers written summaries during consultations. Initial PSA elevation noted in 2022 has progressed to this current clinical review.

DRE: prostate texture symmetric and smooth, devoid of nodularity or asymmetry, aligning with a normal assessment. General examination shows a well-appearing gentleman with a regular heart rhythm at 79 bpm, clear lung fields, blood pressure 133/87 mmHg, and no peripheral oedema.
